title: Same Weight, 0 °C vs 97 °C: Physical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones
subject: Chemistry
objective: Five compounds of the same mass boil from 0 °C to 97 °C. Aldehydes and ketones sit in the middle: their polar C=O gives dipole-dipole attraction, but with no O–H they cannot hydrogen-bond with each other. Water can hydrogen-bond to the C=O oxygen, so small aldehydes and ketones mix with water while long chains do not.

fill.q: The C=O bond is polar: carbon carries a partial ____ charge.
Aldehydes and ketones attract each other by dipole-____ forces.

tf.q: Aldehydes form hydrogen bonds with each other.
tf.explain: They have no O–H, so no H to donate.

tf.q: Propanone mixes with water in all proportions.
tf.explain: It hydrogen-bonds with water through the C=O oxygen.

tf.q: Solubility in water rises as the alkyl chain grows.
tf.explain: The non-polar part grows, so solubility falls.

ar.r: Acetone has no O–H, so it cannot hydrogen-bond with itself.
Water hydrogen-bonds to the carbonyl oxygen.
